summary.intent: Perform principal-engineer level adversarial reviews of the Callisto repo's PRs (PyPI sealed file sets, then fixes for swallowed-error patterns, then a nested-workspace PR stack #241/#242/#244/#245), hunt for systemic issues, and validate another agent's findings.
summary.outcome: Delivered severity-graded findings across several rounds: PyPI hashless confirmation and stale docs, swallowed-error and symlink/atomic-write issues, architectural gaps, and for the final stack two confirmed high-severity npm nested-workspace bugs (wrong publish directory, observe/publish registry mismatch). Recommended holding the stack, and gave a release-notes policy recommendation. No repository changes were made.

repo: Release pipeline has explicit Absent/Exact/Conflict/Indeterminate states, but earlier stages (discovery, graph build) historically treated failed reads as absence; fixes introduced strict_fs, complete-workspace checks, and apply preflight.

Workspace spec (docs/specs/workspace.json ~line 77) and release spec (docs/specs/release.json ~line 284) explicitly mandate some fallbacks (admit-all on malformed membership, generate-notes fallback), so changing them is a product-policy change needing spec and test updates.
Workspace ownership is inferred independently by membership, lockfile refresh, npm publishing and registry observation, which is the root cause of nested-workspace mismatches.
Repo uses AGENTS.md rules (fix sibling bugs together), .agents/skills (bug-hunter, ranger audit, entire-search), and `just ci`; GitHub checks total 12 per PR.
PyPI sealed set: unsealed builds accept hashless index responses as a documented recovery tradeoff; sealed file sets require matching hashes.
Git refuses to stage paths through directory symlinks (exit 128) and ignored files (exit 1), so discovery and preflight must match what Git can stage.

code.finding: Digest comparison only flags a mismatch if the index supplies a SHA-256, so hashless responses are accepted for same-run uploads.
`if let Ok(editor) = open_cached(...)` silently dropped publish targets and dependency edges (also near 727) before the strict graph-completeness fix.
Manifest read errors were treated as 'no manifest here' during discovery.
sync_directory returns success for any directory-open error after rename, so the durability guarantee still has an exception.
npm_workspace_dir recognizes only lockfiles and pnpm-workspace.yaml, not a package.json `workspaces` declaration, so a lockfile-free nested workspace resolves to the repo root.
npm view observation runs from repo root while publish (line ~562) runs from the nested workspace, so nested .npmrc can make them hit different registries.
workspace_manifest_candidates uses the current manifest's package.workspace path for both parent and release commits, which can break release-commit verification when the path changes.
Generated Python-only release job has contents: write with persisted checkout credentials while running the build backend.

workflow: Verify another agent's findings against current source and callers; separate confirmed defects from conditional leads and note overreaching severity claims.
Reproduce suspected behaviors with isolated temp-dir experiments (git add through symlink, ignored file, npm --workspace from different directories, npm config registry) before assigning severity.
Review stacked PRs at each boundary and at combined head, and fetch origin to avoid reviewing stale cached refs.
Use a detached worktree off origin/main to review merged code without disturbing the user's dirty working tree.

friction: gh CLI was initially blocked by network restrictions, forcing local-branch review first.
Local origin/main was stale; remote had moved and required a fetch and detached worktree.
Saved Entire session history was inaccessible, so the assistant could not attribute what Claude had or had not noticed.
Line numbers cited by the other agent were off, requiring re-verification.
Green CI did not cover cross-layer scenarios like lockfile-free nested npm workspaces or nested .npmrc.
open_items: Fix npm nested workspace directory resolution and unify observe/publish directory and registry endpoint; add cross-layer tests.
Add a fixture for Cargo package.workspace path migration across release-commit verification.
Close sync_directory error swallowing in atomic.rs.
Decide release-notes policy: recommended generate when no changelog configured, fail when a configured changelog is missing/unreadable/empty, with release.json spec update.
Python-only generated releases still build inside the write-capable job with persisted Git credentials; isolate the build or defer credentials.
Run a hosted end-to-end exercise of the sealed matrix workflow (build, partial upload, rerun).
Consider trusted publishing (OIDC) for npm and PyPI and streaming hashing for large wheels.
Further triage of `.exists()` sites, Git probe three-state handling, and changeset/tag diagnostics remains for follow-up PRs.
